newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRISH BONDS VOLATILE, FOCUS ON US DATA.
newsitem.headline: IRISH BONDS VOLATILE, FOCUS ON US DATA.

text.p: Irish bonds put in a volatile performance in light trade on Wednesday, losing ground as the day wore after a brief attempt to rally on lower-than-expected U.S. PPI data, dealers said.
"Overall there is not a lot of change in levels against gilts or bunds," one bond dealer said. "If anything we have tightened in a little against the 10-year gilt."
By 1440 GMT, the 6.5 percent the Irish bond due 2001 was down 27 pence on Tuesday's closing level at 102.08 to yield 5.91 percent.
The 8.0 percent bond due 2006 shed 40 pence trading at 110.20 to yield 6.47 percent.
"The U.S. is the focus this week," the dealer said. "The market is moving on a mixture of data and rumour but volumes are low because a lot of people are on holiday."
Irish bonds and gilts got a temporary boost from benign U.S. data which showed producer prices down 0.1 percent in July while retail sales jumped 0.6 percent, slightly below forecast.
Earlier British unemployment data showed that UK wage inflation was static in July while the Bank of England report indicated that a pause in monetary policy should now be possible.

Bunds saw strong gains on the lower-than-expected U.S. PPI data after range-trading most of Wednesday's session following early losses caused by overnight U.S. Treasury weakness and strong words on inflation in a Bundesbank report.

Dealers said with inflation remaining subdued in the U.S. markets will likely breathe a sigh of relief ahead of the August FOMC meeting, although they will be wary about Thursday's release of July CPI and June business inventories.
